text:
ana: quick follow-up on the governance-spine refactor RFC — putting notes and migration Qs here. TL;DR: propose splitting the monolithic governance-spine into two services: governance-eval (stateless evaluator) and governance-store (state + audit). goal is easier scaling for eval-heavy paths and clearer ownership for stateful concerns.

mike: +1 to separation in principle. concerns: cross-service latency and transactional semantics when an eval needs fresh store writes.

sophie: agree with mike. can we avoid sync writes on the critical path? maybe write-behind or causal consistency is enough for most use cases.

ana: (typo) ana: yes — for most decisions we can accept eventual consistency. only a handful of paths need strong consistency (quota depletion, billing-affecting changes). those should route to a small set of endpoints that coordinate a sync write to governance-store.

chris: concrete interface question: do we want eval -> store sync over gRPC or via async queue + policystore sidecar? gRPC is simpler but couples availability. async queue buys resilience but increases complexity and tail latency for edge cases.

mike: prefer gRPC for sync-critical calls and async for all others. that gives us a clear boundary: governance-eval exposes EvalSync(ctx, request) and EvalAsync(ctx, requestId).

ana: sketch of API (very rough):
```
service GovernanceEval {
  rpc EvalSync(EvalRequest) returns (EvalResponse); // low-latency, may call store
  rpc EvalAsync(EvalRequest) returns (Ack); // enqueue for eventual processing
}

// store API
service GovernanceStore {
  rpc GetPolicy(GetPolicyReq) returns (Policy);
  rpc WriteDecision(DecisionWriteReq) returns (WriteAck);
}
```

sophie: ops questions: can we run governance-store on dedicated nodes with local SSD for audit logs? also retention + export pipeline needs to be defined before we cut.

chris: yes to dedicated nodes. retention: default 90d hot, move to cold storage after. export job to S3 nightly. we'll need small-migrations to copy existing audit rows into the new format.

ana: rollout plan idea: 1) implement eval service that reads current store (read-only) 2) launch eval behind a feature flag (traffic shadowing) 3) run for X weeks, compare decisions/latency 4) enable EvalSync for non-critical paths 5) cutover sync-critical paths with canary and rollback hooks.

mike: how do we detect semantic drift between old and new eval? we should record inputs+outputs to a sidecar eval log and run nightly diff job. failure mode: mismatches > 0.1% -> block cutover.

ana: +1. add automatic regression alerting in console with sample traces for mismatches. also suggest tying regression checks to latest model/config changes.

chris: data migration note: we have ~120M audit rows. migration should be chunked by time + tenant to avoid hotspots. include a blackhole mode on migration to re-run if we discover gaps.

sophie: SLOs — governance-eval must keep p50 < 12ms p95 < 40ms for hosted-host path. governance-store p50 < 8ms when on-calls for sync writes (we can accept higher p95 for store but want to cap). we should track tail from downstream callers and surface in console.

ana: ops/observability checklist (short):
- side-by-side decision logging (shadow mode)
- regression diff job + dashboard
- request tracing across eval->store
- canary toggle per-tenant + automatic fallback on errors
- billing+quota guard rails for sync writes

mike: ownership: assign governance-eval to eng-platform (runtime) and governance-store to eng-infra (state + observability). need SLO owner and runbook for both.

chris: security: KV encryption for store, per-tenant keys optional. also audit log immutability requirement for compliance teams — need HSM/KMS integration notes.

ana: open Qs to resolve before RFC -> PR:
- exact contract for EvalSync (idempotency, retry semantics)
- failure modes: what happens when store is down during sync-critical path (circuit-break to fallback decision?)
- migrations: chunking strategy + verification tooling
- canary thresholds and automation for rollback

mike: i'll draft the EvalSync proto with idempotency key pattern. assigning myself for prototype and shadowing run.

sophie: i'll own migration plan + retention/export.

chris: i'll own infra sizing for store and the canary infra (feature flags + rollout automation).

eng-arch-bot: noted: owners assigned (mike/sophie/chris). created ticket INFRA-7241 with patch backlog. :white_check_mark:

ana: awesome — thanks all. @mike please ping when proto's up, i'll wire shadowing. will follow up with a short doc that lists breakpoints for sync vs async decisions. :eyes:
